tasks.title: One module for the gate's paperwork checks, with a stage set per role
tasks.summary: Factory-level. The gate's read-only pre-test checks move into one module, paperwork.ts, with a stage set per hand-off role (coder, tester, grader, gate); the gate calls it stage by stage, a preflight calls it whole, and the gate's behaviour and events are unchanged.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. Create factory/orchestrator/src/paperwork.ts as the single home of the gate's read-only pre-test checks, and make gate.ts and uiuxGate.ts call it, so a preflight (task-2's `bs results check`) and the gate can never disagree on the same input. Today these checks sit inline in gate.ts `runGateStages` (gate.ts:1185-1470, everything before the test stage), interleaved with their `emit` calls, and the private `checkGraderVerdict` (gate.ts:751-835) both validates and emits. Split each into a pure function that returns the verdict plus the exact payload the gate emits today, and keep every `emit` in gate.ts in today's order with today's payload. The paperwork stages, in the gate's order: (1) `schema`, the result record's schema check (`validateRecord`) -> `schema-invalid`; (2) `artifacts`, `checkArtifacts` -> `artifacts-missing`; (3) `commit`, `certifyCommit` -> `not-committed`; (4) `deps`, `checkWorktreeDeps` -> `deps-missing`; (5) `judges`, outstanding judge turns -> `judges-outstanding`; (6) `uiux`, when the task is ui-affecting, the checkUiux verdict -> its four reasons, in checkUiux's order: `uiux-spec-missing`, `screenshots-missing` (no tester record, or a REQUIRED_COMBOS shot missing or not on disk), `screenshots-stale`, `uiux-visual-missing`; (7) `screenshots`, the tester's own declared screenshots (tester role only, below) -> `screenshots-missing`; (8) `grader`, the grader file's shape -> `grader-invalid`. Export `checkPaperwork(input, ctx, opts)` with `input.as: 'coder' | 'tester' | 'grader' | 'gate'`, and an exported `STAGES_FOR_ROLE`. Each role checks only the stages its own hand-off can already satisfy: coder = schema, artifacts, commit, deps; tester = schema, artifacts, screenshots; grader = grader; gate = schema, artifacts, commit, deps, judges, uiux, grader, in the gate's order. For the gate role, `screenshots-missing` is the uiux stage's verdict; stage (7) is the tester's own pre-hand-back check over its declared screenshots and is not in the gate's set; both apply the same screenshot-set function, so the tester and the gate agree on the same shots. Judge turns, the uiux spec and visual turns and the tester record exist only once the wave-runner has dispatched and recorded them, so no worker role checks them. A stage outside the role's set is listed under `skipped` with why `not-checked-for-<role>`; a stage in the set whose input is absent is `skipped` with why `no-input`. The grader stage checks shape only. A well-formed grader file whose verdict is not met, or whose run_status is `dead`, is not a paperwork problem: checkPaperwork reports it as `verdicts.grader: 'fail' | 'not-graded'` and does not block on it, in every role. The gate's own `grader-fail` block is unchanged, so only the verdict, never the paperwork, blocks a task that failed its rubric. `input.alsoReported?: {role, kind}[]` names judge turns the caller is about to close (task-2's gate mode passes the closes its `gate run` line would make); the judges and uiux stages count those turns as reported. checkPaperwork itself closes nothing. Move `SCREENSHOT_RE` and `screenshotsFromArtifacts` (private today, gate.ts:451-453) into paperwork.ts and export both; gate.ts's `recordTaskResult` imports them. In uiuxGate.ts add two exports: a pure `evaluateUiux(events, input, alsoReported?)` holding today's checkUiux logic over a given event list, and a screenshot-set function (the REQUIRED_COMBOS test, uiuxGate.ts:48, plus the on-disk test through `resolveArtifactPath`). `checkUiux` keeps its declaration and becomes readLineage plus evaluateUiux. paperwork.ts's screenshots stage applies the same screenshot-set function to `screenshotsFromArtifacts` of the tester's own declared artifacts, so the tester stage and the gate's uiux stage share one combo implementation. No runtime import cycle: uiuxGate.ts does not import paperwork.ts, and paperwork.ts imports gate.ts for types only; if `checkWorktreeDeps`'s body (gate.ts:1114) moves into paperwork.ts, gate.ts keeps its export with the same declaration and delegates. Stamping the envelope stays in the CLI (results.ts `stampResultEnvelope`, as `gate run` does it today): checkPaperwork takes the complete result document. The test stage, coverage evidence, findings intake and budget check stay in gate.ts alone.
acceptance_criteria: factory/orchestrator/src/paperwork.ts exports `checkPaperwork`, `STAGES_FOR_ROLE`, `SCREENSHOT_RE`, `screenshotsFromArtifacts` and one pure function per stage; uiuxGate.ts adds only `evaluateUiux` and the screenshot-set function. gate.ts's `runGateStages` and `recordTaskResult` and uiuxGate.ts's `checkUiux` call them, and no second copy of the schema, artifact, commit, deps, judges-outstanding, screenshot-combo or grader-shape logic remains in gate.ts or uiuxGate.ts.

Gate parity, in test/paperwork.test.ts, on fixtures built by a new test/helpers/paperworkFixtures.ts: for each fixture `runGate` (with a no-op check command) returns `blocked` with reason R and `checkPaperwork({as: 'gate'})` returns `reason` R. Fixtures: unstamped envelope (a worker half with no task_id/agent/provider/model_tier/token_usage) -> `schema-invalid`; a worker shape error -> `schema-invalid`; a declared artifact never written -> `artifacts-missing`; an artifact path outside the task's artifact home -> `artifacts-missing`; uncommitted work in the worktree -> `not-committed`; a worktree whose deps check fails -> `deps-missing`; a dispatched, unreported judge turn -> `judges-outstanding`; a grader verdict outside `structured_output`, one missing criteria fields, and one with round 3 -> `grader-invalid`; a tester record whose screenshot is named without the `-<desktop|mobile>-<light|dark>.png` suffix, and one with a combo missing -> `screenshots-missing`; no uiux spec turn -> `uiux-spec-missing`; no visual turn after the tester record -> `uiux-visual-missing`. On the clean fixture both pass. The one stated difference, asserted as such: on a well-formed grader `fail` verdict and on a `dead` grader file `runGate` blocks `grader-fail`, while checkPaperwork passes with `verdicts.grader` `fail` and `not-graded`.

Role parity and stage sets: (a) coder: on the unstamped, shape-error, missing-artifact, outside-home, uncommitted and deps fixtures `checkPaperwork({as: 'coder'})` returns the reason `runGate` returns; (b) tester: on a misnamed screenshot, a missing combo, a screenshot declared but not on disk, and a clean tester result, on a session that already has the uiux spec turn, `recordTaskResult` on the tester's result followed by `checkUiux` returns R and `checkPaperwork({as: 'tester'})` on the same result document returns R (`screenshots-missing`, or a pass); (c) on a ui-affecting task with a session where no uiux spec turn, no tester record and no visual turn exist and a judge turn is dispatched and unreported, `as: 'coder'` and `as: 'tester'` on otherwise clean input pass and list judges and uiux under `skipped` with why `not-checked-for-<role>`; `as: 'grader'` skips every stage but grader.

alsoReported: on the judges-outstanding fixture and the uiux-visual-missing fixture, `checkPaperwork({as: 'gate', alsoReported})` naming the open turn passes the judges and uiux stages, and the same call without `alsoReported` blocks with the gate's reason; the events directory is unchanged either way.

Characterization: a test written first, and green on the unchanged code, drives `runGate` on the clean fixture and on the schema-invalid, artifacts-missing, not-committed, grader-invalid and screenshots-missing fixtures and pins the lineage's event types, their order and their payloads; it passes unchanged after the refactor.

Stage-order ladder: one fixture carries every paperwork defect at once. Removing the defects one at a time, `runGate` returns, in order, `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `not-committed`, `deps-missing`, `judges-outstanding`, a uiux reason, `grader-invalid`, then a pass, and `checkPaperwork({as: 'gate'})` returns the same reason at every step. `notes` shows a mutation that swaps two paperwork stages in `runGateStages` failing this test.
checkPaperwork writes nothing: a test runs it in every role on every fixture and compares the events directory and the results directory byte for byte before and after.

A stage is never reported as passed when it did not run: a stage outside the role's set is `skipped` with `not-checked-for-<role>`; a stage in the set with no input is `skipped` with `no-input` (no worktree: commit and deps; no session: judges and uiux; not ui-affecting: uiux; no grader file: grader; no tester screenshots on a task that is not ui-affecting: screenshots). A stage whose input an earlier failure left unreadable is `skipped`, not guessed.
checkPaperwork reports every problem in gate order, not only the first: a fixture with both a schema error and a missing artifact lists both, and `reason` is `schema-invalid`.
This task does not edit test/gate.test.ts, test/uiuxGate.test.ts, test/artifacts.test.ts or test/testgate.test.ts, and every assertion in them still passes.

Diff check (AC8), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|flaky|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (a moved line whose value is unchanged, or prose that forbids the thing). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

functional_clauses: One implementation: each paperwork verdict is computed by a function in paperwork.ts or uiuxGate.ts (or by the existing `checkArtifacts`, `certifyCommit`, `checkWorktreeDeps` and `validateRecord` they call); gate.ts and uiuxGate.ts call the same functions.

Split `checkGraderVerdict` into a pure validator in paperwork.ts that returns the shape verdict (`ok` or `invalid`), the rubric verdict (`met`, `not-met` or `not-graded`) and the payload; gate.ts maps it to `grader-invalid` / `grader-fail` exactly as today, and the `grader-verdict` event's payload is unchanged.
The gate's stage order, every `emit`, every event payload, every blocked reason and the GateOutcome union are unchanged.

`checkPaperwork(input, ctx, opts)` returns `{outcome: 'pass' | 'blocked', reason?, as, problems, skipped, verdicts}`; `reason` is the first blocking reason, in the gate's stage order, among the role's stages, using the gate's own reason strings; a not-met or dead grader verdict is never a blocking reason.
`STAGES_FOR_ROLE` is coder = schema, artifacts, commit, deps; tester = schema, artifacts, screenshots; grader = grader; gate = schema, artifacts, commit, deps, judges, uiux, grader.
`alsoReported` changes only how the judges and uiux stages read turns; it closes, writes and emits nothing.
checkPaperwork writes nothing: no event, no result file, no judge-turn close; the only commands it starts are the read-only git calls `certifyCommit` already makes.
test/helpers/paperworkFixtures.ts exports one builder per fixture in the parity, role and ladder lists, so task-2's CLI tests reuse the same fixtures.
No runtime import cycle between gate.ts, uiuxGate.ts and paperwork.ts.

tasks.title: bs results check: the gate's paperwork before hand-back, per role
tasks.summary: Factory-level. A read-only `bs results check <task-id> --as <coder|tester|grader|gate>` runs checkPaperwork with the role's stage set; gate mode takes the `gate run` line verbatim, parses its files with the gate's own intake, dry-runs its judge closes and runs no check command.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. Add `bs results check <task-id> --as <coder|tester|grader|gate>` to factory/orchestrator/src/cli.ts and its entry to usage.ts COMMANDS. It is the preflight that workers run before hand-back and the wave-runner runs before `gate run`. It calls task-1's `checkPaperwork` with `as` set and adds no validation logic of its own. The task id is positional, as in `gate run`. Role modes (coder, tester, grader) take the flags a worker's brief line carries: `--result <file>` (coder, tester), `--grader <file>` (grader), `--agent <role> --provider <name> --model-tier <tier> [--input-tokens <n> --output-tokens <n>]` stamped through results.ts `stampResultEnvelope` exactly as the `gate run` arm does (cli.ts:3823-3833), `--worktree <dir>` (required for coder), `--base <ref>`, `--plan <plan.json>` (required for tester, read for `ui_affecting` the way `gate run` reads it), `--artifacts-dir <dir>`, and the events-dir and session flags. A role mode refuses every gate-only flag (`--checks`, `--run-all`, `--evidence`, `--found-by`, `--found-by-provider`, `--findings`, `--no-findings`, `--uiux-visual`, `--lessons`) with a usage error naming `--as gate`. Gate mode accepts the `gate run` line verbatim: every flag usage.ts lists for `gate run`, with the same required flags. It reads every file on that line with the gate's own intake functions: `readChecksFile` for `--checks` (cli.ts:352; parsed, never run), `readFindingsInputFile` (cli.ts:312), `evidenceSources` and `mintFromEvidence` (cli.ts:1019, 1061), `mintFromUiuxVisual` (cli.ts:1084), `parseLessons`, and the `--grader` file. It never spawns a check. Judge-close dry run: `gate run` closes the judge turns its own line hands in before the gate's judges stage (cli.ts:3874-3901, and `--no-findings` at cli.ts:3909-3921), so a read-only preflight must know which closes that line would make and whether each would succeed. Extract the selection of those closes (the same closeKey rule: once per role and kind, only for an unreported turn of that role and kind) into one helper in cli.ts that both arms call. Extract from judges.ts `recordJudgeReport` (judges.ts:921) everything it checks before it appends (the kind check, turn selection, artifact freshness, `readJudgeArtifact`) into a new exported `checkJudgeReport(input, turns, opts)` that throws the same JudgeError codes and appends nothing; `recordJudgeReport` keeps its declaration and calls it. results check runs `checkJudgeReport` for each selected close: a throw is a blocked problem under its own code, and each close that would succeed is passed to checkPaperwork as `alsoReported`. Output, on stdout, one JSON document: `{outcome: 'pass' | 'blocked', reason?, as, task_id, artifact_home, problems, skipped, not_run, verdicts?, warnings}`. `not_run` names the gate stages a preflight never evaluates (`tests`, `coverage-evidence`, `findings`, `budget`). `artifact_home` is the absolute directory the artifact stage resolved, so a worker can see it is the one the gate will read. Exit 0 only on pass and 1 on blocked. A usage error or refusal exits 1 through the CLI's existing top-level error document `{error: {code, message, details}}` (cli.ts:5403-5420); there is no other exit code. An intake failure on a file the caller handed in is a blocked problem with a named reason, never a stack trace: `result-unreadable` (missing file, invalid JSON), `results.not-an-object`, `results.agent-wrote-owned-field`, `results.partial-token-count`, `results.invalid-token-count`, `artifacts.missing-task-id`, `artifacts.unsafe-task-id`, and any other SmithError or JudgeError code an intake function throws. A complete result document (no `--agent`) whose `task_id` differs from the positional id adds a `warnings` entry and does not block, as in the gate, which checks artifacts against its own task id (gate.ts:1228-1231). It writes nothing: no event, no result file, no judge-turn close. `bs uiux check` is unchanged; usage.ts says `results check --as gate` includes the uiux stage.
acceptance_criteria: Gate-mode CLI parity in test/cliResultsCheck.test.ts: on every fixture from task-1's test/helpers/paperworkFixtures.ts, `gate run` and `results check --as gate`, run through the built CLI from the worktree as cwd with the same flag list (the gate line copied verbatim, `--checks` a no-op file, the same `--artifacts-dir`), give the same blocking reason, and the clean fixture exits 0 in both. The one stated difference, asserted as such: on the grader `fail` and `dead` fixtures `gate run` blocks `grader-fail` while `results check` exits 0 with `verdicts.grader` `fail` / `not-graded`.

Judge-close dry run: on a fixture with a dispatched, unreported grader turn and `--grader <file>` on the line, and on one with a dispatched, unreported uiux visual turn and `--uiux-visual <file>` on the line, `gate run` closes the turn and passes the judges and uiux stages, and `results check --as gate` with the same line passes them too while the events directory stays byte-identical. A handed-in file that `gate run` fails to close on (stale, missing, invalid evidence) blocks `results check` under the same JudgeError code `gate run` fails with. test/judgeReportCheck.test.ts shows `checkJudgeReport` throws exactly where `recordJudgeReport` throws, with the same code, and appends nothing; every existing judges test passes unchanged.

Role modes: `--as coder` on task-1's coder fixtures returns the reason `gate run` returns; `--as tester --plan <plan>` returns `screenshots-missing` on the misnamed, missing-combo and not-on-disk screenshot fixtures and passes a clean tester result on a ui-affecting task whose uiux spec turn, tester record and visual turn do not exist yet; `--as grader --grader <file>` returns `grader-invalid` on the three shape fixtures and exits 0 with `verdicts.grader` on the `fail` and `dead` fixtures. Each role mode refuses each gate-only flag with a usage error naming `--as gate`; `--as coder` without `--worktree` and `--as tester` without `--plan` are usage errors.

Envelope: without `--agent/--provider/--model-tier` a worker half blocks `schema-invalid` in both verbs; with them, the same file passes `results check --as coder`. With those flags on both lines, a worker half that sets a dispatcher-owned field makes `gate run` fail with error code `results.agent-wrote-owned-field` (results.ts `stampResultEnvelope`) and makes `results check` block with that reason.

Malformed and hostile input: a missing result file, invalid JSON, a JSON array, a result whose `artifacts` is not an array, a positional task id `../x` and a blank task id each make `results check` exit 1 with one JSON document on stdout (blocked with the named reason, or the CLI's `{error: {code}}` document for a usage error), never a stack trace and never a pass. A complete result whose `task_id` differs from the positional id produces a `warnings` entry, and its artifacts are checked against the positional id's home, as the gate checks them.

Artifact home: both verbs run from the worktree cwd with the same `--artifacts-dir`, and `results check` prints `artifact_home` equal to the directory the gate's artifact check resolved; with no `--artifacts-dir`, both resolve the same home from the same environment.

Read-only: in every mode on every fixture, the events directory and the results directory are byte-identical before and after `results check`; the worktree's `git status --porcelain` output is unchanged, read by the test as `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain` so the proof itself never refreshes the index; the bytes of the worktree's git index file (the path `git rev-parse --git-path index` prints) are identical before and after; and no `index.lock` exists beside it afterwards. The verb's own commit-stage `git status` must not refresh the index either (for example `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` for the verb's run); commit.ts is outside this task's claims and stays unchanged.

Runs no test command: given a worktree whose package.json test script and whose checks-file command each write a marker file, `results check --as gate --checks <that file>` leaves no marker and lists `tests` under `not_run`.

uiux relationship: `bs uiux check` is unchanged, and on the uiux-spec-missing, screenshots-missing, screenshots-stale and uiux-visual-missing fixtures `uiux check --task --plan --worktree` and `results check --as gate` with the same plan and worktree return the same reason.

usage.ts lists `results check` with `--as` and every flag per mode, and says gate mode includes the uiux stage; the `gate run` entry is unchanged; test/usage.test.ts and test/docCommands.test.ts pass.

Exit codes and output: 0 only on pass, 1 on blocked or refused, nothing else. The output is one JSON document with `outcome`, `reason` (blocked only), `as`, `task_id`, `artifact_home`, `problems`, `skipped`, `not_run`, `warnings`, and `verdicts` when a grader file was read.

Diff check (AC8), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|flaky|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (a moved line whose value is unchanged, or prose that forbids the thing). An unexplained hit fails this criterion.

One close-selection helper in cli.ts, called by both `gate run` and `results check`; `gate run` makes exactly the closes it makes today.
`checkJudgeReport` is extracted from `recordJudgeReport`, which keeps its declaration and behaviour and calls it; no check is duplicated between them.

tasks.title: The gate records sleep evidence on a failed test run
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Each gate check records wall-clock and monotonic time, their gap, and the load average; a failed check whose own clock gap shows the machine slept stays blocked as tests-failed and is classified execution.env-failure. Load is evidence only. Nothing is re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts, measure around each check command: wall-clock ms, monotonic ms, their gap, the 1-minute load average at start and at end, and the CPU count. Put them on each CheckResult as an optional `environment` object that `run` always sets (optional on the type so integration.ts and other constructors compile unchanged). The clock and load sources are injectable through RunOptions and GateInput, with today's real sources as the default. Export a pure classifier and one named constant, `SLEEP_GAP_MS = 30_000`. The classifier fires on the clock gap only: `clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`. Node's monotonic clock (`process.hrtime`, libuv's uv_hrtime) does not advance while the machine is suspended on the platforms the factory runs on (macOS `mach_absolute_time`, Linux `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), while the wall clock does, so the gap measures time asleep; a check cannot put the machine to sleep, so a failing suite cannot cause its own classification. 30 s is far above NTP slew and below any real suspend worth naming; the constant's comment says so and names its source. On a platform whose monotonic clock counts suspend, the gap reads about 0 and the classifier never fires, which fails safe as a plain tests-failed block. Load is recorded as evidence only and never classifies: a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself, so a load threshold would label real failures as environment failures. In gate.ts, when the test stage fails, run the classifier over each failed check's own evidence; a gap on a check that passed never classifies another check's failure. When it fires, the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned blocked GateOutcome each carry `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` and the failed check's evidence. The outcome stays `blocked`, the reason stays `tests-failed`, nothing is re-run, and the gate finalizes exactly as for any other tests-failed block. A run that passes is never classified, whatever its evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every CheckResult from `run` carries `environment: {wall_ms, monotonic_ms, clock_gap_ms, load_1m_start, load_1m_end, cpus}`; a test in test/testgate.test.ts with an injected clock and load source pins each value exactly.

Classifier boundary tests: a clock gap of `SLEEP_GAP_MS - 1` does not fire and one of `SLEEP_GAP_MS` does; a load per CPU of 100 at start and at end with a gap of 0 does not fire. `SLEEP_GAP_MS` is exported, named, and commented with the source of its value; no load threshold exists.

tasks.title: Two named tests stop racing a timer
tasks.summary: Repo-level. The daemon per-tick CLI test and the cli-transport process-group timeout test no longer race the code's own timer; every behaviour they pinned stays pinned and no production file changes.
tasks.objective: Repo-level fix for this repo's two named recurring test failures. Test files only; no production file changes. (a) test/cli.test.ts, 'prints one report per tick as it runs, and a count with no report at the end': today it needs two real ticks, `--interval 1` apart, inside `waitForLines`' 15 s wait. Run the daemon with an interval long enough that no second tick can start during the test, wait for the first line only, send SIGTERM during the sleep, and require exit status 0, empty stderr, no `daemon.pid`, and the closing line `{ticks: 1, dir}`. This also pins that SIGTERM reaches the sleep. The repeat (one report per tick, each handed out before the sleep) is already pinned in-process in test/daemon.test.ts ('hands each report to onTick before the sleep, and keeps none of them'). Confirm that it pins every per-tick behaviour the CLI test's second line pinned, and add an in-process assertion to daemon.test.ts for any it does not. The `--interval` value is the daemon's tick gap under test, not a test deadline. (b) test/providers/cli-transport.test.ts, 'times out and kills the WHOLE process group, not just the immediate child': today a real 200 ms timer can fire before the fixture has spawned its grandchild and written grandchild.pid. Keep `timeout_ms: 200` and fire it only once grandchild.pid holds a pid. The timer is the global `setTimeout` armed in src/spawn.ts:80 (`spawnCapped`), reached through `spawnOnce` (src/providers/cli-transport.ts:60-66, which arms no timer of its own); `killGroup` (src/spawn.ts:70-78) sends SIGKILL with no grace timer. So `vi.useFakeTimers({toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout']})`, installed before the `runCliJudge` call, captures that timer and nothing else the call needs. Without advancing the fake clock, read and parse grandchild.pid through `setImmediate` polling (not faked) until it holds a positive integer pid; a missing or still-empty file means keep polling, never advance (read and parse, never mere existence). The poll races the pending `runCliJudge` promise: attach a settle handler to that promise when the call is made, and if it settles (resolves or rejects) before a parseable pid appears, because the fake-judge child died or exited early, the test fails at once with an assertion that says so (for example 'runCliJudge settled before grandchild.pid held a pid') instead of polling until the test timeout. No extra deadline is needed and none is added: vitest arms each test's timeout with the timers it saved before any fakes were installed, so `vi.useFakeTimers` cannot freeze it and the poll cannot hang past the unchanged test timeout. Then `vi.advanceTimersByTime(200)`, await the `provider.timeout` rejection, and restore real timers in a `finally` before the liveness wait, which checks the parsed pid. Add an optional start delay to the fixture's `slow-grandchild` mode (default 0, every other mode unchanged) and a second case that delays the grandchild by more than `timeout_ms` and still passes. Under fake time the fixture's real start delay cannot make the 200 ms timer fire early, which is what makes the delayed case meaningful: with real timers that case kills the group before the grandchild exists. No production seam is added.
acceptance_criteria: The daemon CLI test waits for one line only, sends SIGTERM during the sleep, and requires exit status 0, empty stderr, no `daemon.pid` and the closing line `{ticks: 1, dir}`; its pass no longer depends on a second interval elapsing inside the wait.
Every behaviour the old two-line daemon test pinned is still pinned, in test/cli.test.ts or in-process in test/daemon.test.ts; `notes` lists each old assertion and the assertion that now pins it.

In `factory/orchestrator/test/providers/cli-transport.test.ts`, the process-group timeout test keeps `timeout_ms: 200`, fakes only `setTimeout`/`clearTimeout` from before the `runCliJudge` call until the rejection, and advances the fake clock by 200 ms only once grandchild.pid holds a parseable positive integer pid: the test reads and parses the file each time it looks, so a missing file, or one that exists but is still empty, never triggers the advance (read and parse, never mere existence); if the pending `runCliJudge` promise settles before a parseable pid appears, the test fails at once with an assertion saying so, never polling until the test timeout. It still requires `provider.timeout` and a dead grandchild, checked on that parsed pid; a second case whose fixture delays the grandchild by more than `timeout_ms` (real time, in the child) passes the same assertions.
No production file changes; `waitForLines`' 15 000 ms default, `testTimeout`, `hookTimeout` and every `timeout_ms` in these tests are unchanged.

Each changed test is shown to fail on the old race: `notes` reports the old test failing under the artificial delay (the fixture delay for (b); a delayed first tick or a SIGTERM after a second tick started for (a)) and the new test passing under the same delay.

Spec review round 1, task-3:criterion-3 (S2), resolved, with one part pushed back. Resolved: the classifier now fires on the failed check's own clock gap only (`clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`, 30 s). Node's monotonic clock does not advance during suspend on macOS (mach_absolute_time) or Linux (CLOCK_MONOTONIC) while the wall clock does, so the gap cannot be caused by the check itself; the threshold is far above NTP slew; a platform whose monotonic clock counts suspend reads a gap of about 0 and never classifies, which fails safe. Load is recorded as evidence only, because a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself. A gap on a passing check never classifies another check's failure. Pushed back: 'never classify when the output shows real assertion failures'. The gate runs arbitrary project commands with no common assertion format (testgate.ts `run` takes any CheckCommand), and a test timed out by a suspend is itself reported as an assertion failure, so output parsing would either miss every real sleep or need per-runner parsers. The classification never passes the block (outcome blocked, reason tests-failed, nothing re-run), and task-4 sends a second env-classified block at the same HEAD to the operator, so a masked real failure cannot leave the queue unseen.

Spec review round 1, task-5:criterion-3 (S2), pushed back; the criterion is buildable and the plan now says how. The finding says the 200 ms timer cannot be made to fire only after grandchild.pid exists without a production change. It can: the timer is the global `setTimeout` armed in spawnCapped (src/spawn.ts:80), reached through spawnOnce (src/providers/cli-transport.ts:60-66, no timer of its own), and killGroup sends SIGKILL with no grace timer (src/spawn.ts:70-78), so `vi.useFakeTimers({toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout']})` captures that one timer and the test advances it by 200 ms once the pid file exists. The finding's second point, that a delay longer than timeout_ms kills the group before the pid is written, holds only for real timers, which is the old race the delayed case exists to show. The objective now names this mechanism and drops the 'stop and report' fallback; criterion 3 says the fake clock is installed before the call and advanced only after the pid file exists.

Plan quorum round 3 (events #19, #21, decision #22), task-5, fixed in round 4: the objective's wait said `existsSync` while criterion-3 said read and parse, and no fast failure was named. The objective and criterion-3 (edited in place, no criterion added) now both say read and parse grandchild.pid until it holds a positive integer pid, never mere existence, and fail at once, saying so, if the pending `runCliJudge` promise settles first. The round-1 note above that says 'once the pid file exists' is superseded by this wording. No new deadline and no raised or added timeout: vitest 5.0.3's per-test timeout cannot be frozen by `vi.useFakeTimers`, because `TaskDeadline` arms it through `getSafeTimers().setTimeout` (node_modules/.pnpm/vitest@5.0.3_*/node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/run.BTlFXlnv.js:3185-3192, used by `withTimeout` at :3253), and `getSafeTimers` reads the globals vitest saved before any fakes were installed (source-map.DUxvo12T.js:894-913). So the poll is bounded by the unchanged test timeout, and the settle race turns the early-exit case into a named failure instead of a timeout.
